property_summary: After two fallback calls with 10 ether each, the reference sets pastBlockTime to timestamp+1, while the bug sets it to timestamp, so after two calls with block.timestamp increasing by 1 each second, the second call reverts on reference but succeeds on bug.

After a fallback call with 10 ether sets pastBlockTime to timestamp+1 (reference) or timestamp (bug), a second call 1 second later reverts on reference due to require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) failing, but succeeds on bug.

After two fallback calls with msg.value = 10 ether at the same block timestamp, the reference contract updates pastBlockTime to timestamp+1 on the first call and reverts on the second (since block.timestamp is not > pastBlockTime), but the buggy version accepts the second call (block.timestamp >= pastBlockTime) and overwrites pastBlockTime to the same value, so P.pastBlockTime() == oldTimestamp+1 while M.pastBlockTime() == oldTimestamp+1 (the buggy version doesn't change pastBlockTime between calls because both calls happen at the same timestamp, but the reference reverts the second call so pastBlockTime stays at oldTimestamp+1; actually the reference second call reverts so pastBlockTime remains from first call, while buggy version second call succeeds and also sets it to block.timestamp+1 which is the same value, so pastBlockTime is equal; need a different scenario where the buggy version overwrites with a different value). Correct scenario: first call at time T sets pastBlockTime = T+1; second call at the same time T reverts in reference (T >= T+1? No, T < T+1, so reference requires >, so T > T+1? false — revert), but buggy accepts (T >= T+1? false — actually T >= T+1 is false because T < T+1, so both would revert? Wait: initial pastBlockTime is 0. First call at T=100, require(block.timestamp > 0) passes, set pastBlockTime = 101. Second call at same T=100, require(block.timestamp > 101) fails in reference (revert), but require(block.timestamp >= 101) also fails (100 >= 101 false). So buggy also reverts. Need a difference: after first call, pastBlockTime = 101. If second call at T=101, reference requires 101 > 101? false (revert), buggy requires 101 >= 101? true (pass). So: first call at T=100, set pastBlockTime=101; second call at T=101, reference reverts, buggy accepts and sets pastBlockTime=102. So P.pastBlockTime == 101, M.pastBlockTime == 102. That diverges.

After two fallback calls with msg.value = 10 ether at block timestamps 100 and 101, the reference contract reverts on the second call (keeping pastBlockTime = 101), while the buggy contract accepts the second call and sets pastBlockTime = 102.

After two fallback calls with msg.value=10 ether at block.timestamp=100 and block.timestamp=101, the reference contract reverts the second call (keeping pastBlockTime=101), while the buggy contract accepts it (setting pastBlockTime=102); we observe the divergence by checking c.pastBlockTime() after the sequence.

After a first call making block.timestamp exactly pastBlockTime+1, the buggy contract allows a second call (in the same block) to succeed because it misses updating pastBlockTime, while the reference reverts. The divergence is shown by calling two fallbacks in a row without block increment: the first with value 10 ether succeeds for both; the second also with 10 ether should revert in reference but passes in buggy.

After a fallback call with exactly 10 ether when block.number is not a multiple of 15, the reference sets pastBlockTime to block.timestamp+1 and the bug sets it to block.timestamp+2, so reading c.pastBlockTime() after the call returns different values.
